title: Uptime Foundry: Cross-functional Reliability Sprint & SLO Activation Plan
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the cross-functional sprint plan for the "Uptime Foundry" initiative: a concentrated 6-week effort to define, instrument, and activate service-level objectives (SLOs) for Redwood’s inference surfaces and to deliver the minimal ops + product artifacts needed for safe rollouts. The plan emphasizes low-friction collaboration between SRE, Serving Runtime, Infra, Product (Hosted API), Console, and Solutions Eng.

Primary objectives:
- Define baseline SLOs and error-budget policies for the Hosted API and Dedicated inference routes.
- Instrument production telemetry and create repeatable dashboards/alerts for SLO measurement.
- Implement canary rollout process and a standard SLO activation checklist.
- Ship runbooks and a training session for on-call and systems owners.

Scope (in):
- SLOs: availability and request-success-rate, and p95/p99 user-facing latency for generation/chat routes.
- Instrumentation: metrics (request_count, error_count, latency_histogram, kv-cache-hit, model-fallbacks), traces (sampled end-to-end), and synthetic probes.
- Dashboards: per-route SLO view, error-budget burn, recent incidents with timeline, and per-model performance splits.
- Alerting: error budget burn alerts and SLO-threshold paging rules.
- Canary system: automated small-rollout with health gates tied to SLO signals.

Out of scope (out):
- Rewriting large portions of the serving runtime.
- Full fleet autoscaler redesign.
- Enterprise-specific private deployment SLOs (these will be follow-ups).

Proposed SLO drafts (for review):
- Hosted API availability: 99.95% monthly for the default text-generation route (excluding scheduled maintenance windows).
- Error rate SLO: successful-response-rate >= 99.9% (client-visible 5xx and malformed output counted as failures).
- Latency SLO (user-facing): p95 < 250ms, p99 < 700ms for short-context text generation (<= 256 tokens). For long-running streams and embeddings, use separate SLOs with relaxed bounds.
- Model-fallback goal: when a primary model fails, fallback response < 2000ms and success rate >= 98% for fallback cases.

Measurement & telemetry plan:
- Metric owners: Serving Runtime team will own instrumentation of request_count, latency_histogram buckets, and error classification tags. Infra will own probe health and K8s-level node metrics. Console team will own the SLO dashboard wiring.
- Data sources: Prometheus for high-cardinality counters, Loki for logs, Tempo for traces, and synthetic probes from 3 regions.
- Tagging conventions: route=<route>, model=<model>, customer_tier=<tier>, deployment_zone=<zone>, canary=true|false. Follow existing metric naming with "redwood_" prefix.

Dashboards & alerts:
- Deliverables: SLO summary dashboard, per-route heatmap, incident timeline panel, error-budget burn rate widget.
- Alerting thresholds: page SRE on SLO burn > 30% in 1 hour AND projected monthly breach; page product owners on sustained p99 breaches for 1 hour.

Runbooks and operational playbooks:
- Minimal runbook template to ship with SLO activation: detection, triage checklist, mitigation playbook (scale up, reject trailing requests, model-variant fallback), rollback steps, postmortem checklist.
- Add runbook snippets to the oncall playbook with links to the SLO dashboard and to specific runbooks per route.

Canary & rollout policy:
- Canary window: 30 minutes per canary stage with automated health checks against p95 latency, error-rate, and synthetic probe pass rate.
- Gates: if canary loses >10% of success-rate or p99 increases by >2x, auto-stop and revert. Manual review if error budget burn is observed.
- Rollout steps: staged traffic split (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated pauses and telemetry validation.

Roles & responsibilities (RACI-style):
- SRE (Asha Patel): Accountable for defining error-budget policies, oncall runbook, and alert paging logic.
- Serving Runtime (Ravi Singh): Responsible for metric instrumentation and model-fallback telemetry.
- Infra (Daniel Kim): Responsible for synthetic probes, infra-level metrics, and capacity knobs for emergency scale.
- Product - Hosted API (Clara Martinez): Responsible for SLO alignment with product SLAs and customer communication templates.
- Console/Observability (Liam O'Connor): Responsible for building SLO dashboards and alert subscriptions.
- Solutions Eng / CS (Maya Chen): Consulted for customer-critical routes and rollout impacts.

Timeline (6 weeks, 3 two-week sprints):
- Sprint 0 (Week 0–1, discovery & quick wins): finalize SLO definitions; instrument basic latency/error metrics for top 3 routes; create initial SLO dashboard wireframe; draft runbook template.
- Sprint 1 (Week 2–3): complete instrumentation for top 8 routes; implement synthetic probes in 3 regions; build error-budget burn alerts and basic canary automation; internal dry-run on staging.
- Sprint 2 (Week 4–5): run limited production canaries on low-traffic subset; iterate dashboards based on oncall feedback; publish runbooks and schedule oncall training.
- Closure week (Week 6): full activation for selected routes, post-activation retro, and create follow-up backlog for enterprise/private SLOs.

Dependencies & enablers:
- Infra capacity to support synthetic probes and additional metrics retention.
- Small changes to runtime to add tags and histogram buckets (backwards compatible).
- Console/observability capacity to build and ship SLO dashboard panels.
- Product sign-off on SLO thresholds and customer communication language.

Risk register (top 6 risks & mitigations):
- Risk: Instrumentation gaps leading to unreliable SLO signals. Mitigation: run parallel synthetic checks and sampling of traces; allocate a 2-day sprint buffer for metric fixes.
- Risk: Canary automation false positives during diurnal load. Mitigation: include baseline-of-day normalization and compare relative windows.
- Risk: Pager noise from immature alerts. Mitigation: use escalations to reduce paging; default to SRE-only first-alert for 2 weeks.
- Risk: Customer pushback on new SLOs. Mitigation: product-led communications, opt-in beta for enterprise customers.
- Risk: Capacity constraints during emergency scale. Mitigation: pre-defined capacity reserve, and temporary traffic-shaping policy.

Communication & stakeholder plan:
- Weekly stakeholder sync: 30 minutes with SRE, runtime, infra, console, and product (Tuesdays 10am PT).
- Twice-weekly status notes in #reliability (Slack) with a concise progress line, blockers, and ask.
- Draft customer-facing FAQ and SLO page for Product to review by end of Sprint 1.

Acceptance criteria (for the initial activation):
- SLO dashboards show <5% data loss for the last 30 days.
- Canary automation executed without manual intervention in at least 80% of test runs on staging.
- Oncall runbook attached and tested during a scheduled fire-drill.
- Error-budget alerts triggered as expected in a synthetic burn test.
- Product owner sign-off and an internal announcement scheduled.

Next steps (week-by-week immediate actions):
- Day 0–2: final SLO thresholds meeting (Asha + Clara + Ravi). Add thresholds to this doc and Confluence.
- Day 3–7: runtime team to push histogram buckets and tags to staging. Infra to stand up probes. Console to scaffold dashboard.
- Week 2: first internal dry-run of canary; SRE to review alert noise and tune thresholds.

Appendix: example Jira tasks to create for the board:
- REL-101: Add redwood_latency_histogram to serving runtime (include buckets for 50/95/99). Assignee: Ravi Singh.
- REL-102: Create synthetic probe job across us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1. Assignee: Daniel Kim.
- REL-103: Build SLO summary dashboard and error-budget widgets. Assignee: Liam O'Connor.
- REL-104: Draft Hosted API SLO customer comms and FAQ. Assignee: Clara Martinez.
- REL-105: Canary automation pipeline and health-gate logic. Assignee: SRE Engineer (TBD).

Notes & open questions:
- Do we include dedicated customer routes in the initial activation or run a parallel pilot? Recommend parallel pilot post-initial activation.
- Should we expose SLOs directly to customers via Console or only publish docs initially? Product preference needed.

This is a working plan — please comment inline and add any missing dependencies or owners. After sign-off we will map these tasks into the REL Jira board and lock the sprint cadence.
